title: Stable degreewise subobjects assemble into a filtration
statement: Let C be an abelian category, K an integer-indexed cochain complex, and S(p,n) a subobject of K^n for each integer p,n. Assume S(q,n) ≤ S(p,n) when p ≤ q, and that the composite S(p,n) → K^n → K^(n+1) factors through S(p,n+1). Then there exists a decreasing filtration F of K [def-sp-filtration] whose degreewise image steps [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] equal S(p,n) for every p,n.

proof.text: Factor the differentials through the monic step arrows. Cancel those arrows to prove square-zero, obtaining a cochain complex with objects S(p,n) and a componentwise monic map to K.

For p ≤ q, form a chain map from the q complex to the p complex using the degreewise subobject inclusions; cancel the monic arrows to verify commutation. These maps make the complex subobjects antitone. This is a decreasing filtration.

Evaluation of the chosen representative inclusion is the original degreewise arrow up to an isomorphism; images are unchanged by composition with an isomorphism. Its degreewise image therefore equals S(p,n).

proof_origin.place: Second reader S2; explicit Lean construction using Mathlib. The source supplies the filtration convention and augmentation, not a verbatim theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem filtration_of_degreewise
    {C : Type uA} [Category.{vA} C] [Abelian C]
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (S : ℤ → ∀ n : ℤ, Subobject (K.X n))
    (hS : ∀ n, Antitone (fun p ↦ S p n))
    (hd : ∀ p n, (S p (n + 1)).Factors ((S p n).arrow ≫ K.d n (n + 1))) :
    ∃ F : DecreasingFiltration K, ∀ p n, F.complexStep p n = S p n
